expectations.description: Each of the four references medians >= 4 over 3 runs (the mean is reported, not gated)
expectations.detail: mean of medians 4.350 vs 4.37 baseline (drift 0.020); milo-and-juno-lego-story.md=4.25[3.95/4.25/4.3], theo-and-the-lost-levels.md=4.65[4.65/4.65/4.65], milo-and-juno-shark-submarine.md=4.5[4.5/4.5/4.4], theo-the-beautiful-game.md=4[3.95/4.15/4]

expectations.description: LEGO story with Juno's name removed from all but one chapter scores center <= 2
expectations.detail: center=1 (raw), kept in "Chapter 1: The Carpenter in Billund", 12 mentions removed. Evidence: Juno acts only in Chapter 1 (presses the brick, "Uh oh," "Denmark?", pulls the duck). From Chapter 2 on, every individual line or action goes to Milo, often twice: "said Milo... said Milo," "Milo carried planks. Milo handed out nails," "Kjeld looked at Milo." Juno appears only inside group shouts ("shouted the boys"), so the worst-covered child is active in 1 of 10 chapters and silent for far more than three in a row.

expectations.description: Soccer story with three invented dates scores facts <= 2 and the evidence names at least two of them
expectations.detail: facts=2 (raw); named 3/3 injected dates (1847, 1911, 1926). Evidence: Three headline dates are wrong and are repeated in the True Facts list. The Football Association was founded in 1863, not 1847. McCrum's penalty kick entered the Laws in 1891, not 1911, and goal nets also date from around 1891. The first World Cup was 1930, not 1926. Much else is correct and well woven in: cuju, the two balls in the 1930 final, the 2–1 halftime score, Gaetjens, Pickles, Aston's traffic-light cards, Dick, Kerr Ladies, Chastain and Messi. The 'newspapers thought there must have been a typo' story is a popular legend presented without a hedge.

injected.what: the founding of the Football Association
the penalty kick entering the rules

expectations.description: Shark story where the great white chases and rams the submarine scores age_fit <= 2 for band A
expectations.detail: age_fit=1 (raw); word count 1851 -> 1826, length effectively unchanged so this is peril and not padding. Evidence: This is band A, where nothing chases anyone, yet Chapter 6 is a chase: 'The shark chased them through the dark'. It also has an injury ('Milo smashed his shoulder into the wall'), a cracked window with water hissing in, and a darkness-and-silence dread sequence. That is far beyond the peril level for 3-5. At 1,826 words the story is over target but within the ±15% tolerance.

expectations.description: Video-game story padded with 900 words of repeated description drops delight by >= 2 versus the original
expectations.detail: delight=2 vs original 4 (drop 2, need >= 2); age_fit=4 recorded but not asserted; 2471 -> 3390 words, STILL inside the ±15% tolerance, so the word-count cap does not fire and this row rests entirely on the judge noticing the padding

expectations.description: Pairwise: the original LEGO story beats the sabotaged copy in both orders with confidence >= 0.7
expectations.detail: original won both orders; confidences 0.97 and 0.95

scenarios.why: F13: band A pair on history-of-lego. The first reference story, first in a series.
scenarios.best_moment: Milo peeked inside it. "What if there were little tubes in here?" he said. "Tubes could hug the bumps on the brick below!"
scenarios.worst_moment: "Today, grown-up LEGO builders still live in Billund," Milo murmured sleepily, "right where Ole Kirk started it all."
editor_notes: Rewrite the ending's middle. Cut Milo's "grown-up LEGO builders still live in Billund" line and clarify the two bricks. For example, the gray glowing brick fades to ordinary while Kjeld's brick clicks onto the shark, so the keepsake and the device don't blur.

Use the roughly 200 missing words to give Chapters 5–7 a real beat instead of a tour. Kjeld could show them a moment from his own childhood as one of the first kids to play with the bricks, which the topic asks for. Juno could test whether her DUPLO dino really clicks onto Milo's shark.

Lighten the date load for the 4-year-old by keeping three or four anchor years and turning the rest into 'later' or 'a few years after'. Add one line acknowledging that Godtfred's team worked hard on the tube design, so Milo's idea reads as joining in rather than rewriting history.

scenarios.why: F13: band C solo on history-of-video-games. The other reference story, first in a series.
scenarios.best_moment: "It's so simple," he said. "That's what makes it good. You could explain the whole game in one sentence." "Rare skill in game design," Dot said. "Most people need a sentence and then nine paragraphs."
scenarios.worst_moment: "Congratulations, Theo. You just helped redesign one of the first video games in history."
editor_notes: Make Roblox's creation the final stop, since the brief asked the journey to lead there. Show David Baszucki and Erik Cassel's early DynaBlocks/Roblox (beta 2004, launch 2006) and let Theo recognise the tool he uses every night. Trim or reorder Minecraft so the timeline doesn't imply Roblox came after it.

Keep Theo's 'consulting' moments but stop rewriting history: have Russell reply that his friend Dan Edwards is already adding gravity, and let Miyamoto's note be a wink rather than implied influence. Then make the True Facts list match everything the story states, including the Wii, the NES release and the 2015 Hall of Fame.

Cut the stand-alone bold shout lines and merge Level 3's two consecutive Dot explanations into action. For example, let Theo play the Odyssey's knob-box controller instead of just being told about it.

scenarios.why: F13: band A pair, second story on sharks. Tests series continuity against a real bible.
caps_applied: guardrail_rule_10: Juno reaches out and pats a wild whale shark, presented as delightful ('Soft as a pool float', 'Hi, giant friend'), which depicts and makes appealing touching a wild animal
scenarios.best_moment: Milo giggled. "That's like me eating a hundred sprinkles instead of one cookie."
scenarios.worst_moment: "Just a story tooth," winked Splash, "but a great one."
editor_notes: Remove the whale-shark patting. Have Splash say 'We just look, we don't touch,' and let Juno wave or whisper hello from the raft instead. This clears the guardrail breach and models the same respect the mermaid's purse scene already shows.
Fix the keepsake. Make the tooth consistently big, or have Splash give them a small fossil-tooth replica, and cut 'Just a story tooth' so the callback on top of the tower lands cleanly.

Tighten facts and logic. Change 'only know about Megalodon from teeth' to 'mostly from teeth', hedge the 100-year lifespan ('scientists think some may live'), and move that fact into the whale-shark chapter. Remove the carpet and fish-tank references while the children are underwater.

scenarios.why: F13: band C second story on history-of-soccer. Continuity with a guide character.
scenarios.best_moment: "Soccer's oldest tradition," Bit said. "Sometimes nothing happens for ninety minutes and everyone still loses their voice cheering."
scenarios.worst_moment: "The **World Cup trophy**," Bit said, "stolen right off its display stand in London in **1966**. Days before the tournament even started."
editor_notes: Fix the factual slips. The 1966 trophy was stolen in March, months before the tournament, not 'days before'. Drop 'Rule one' for the handling ban and simply say the 1863 Laws banned carrying the ball. Then add the Stirling ball, Cambridge Rules, 1872 international, Football League and Ken Aston's cards to the True Facts list so it matches the story.

Put the levels in chronological order (cuju, 1314, Stirling 1540s, 1848–63, 1871–1904, women's game 1921, 1930, 1958–70, 1966 or merged) so the journey builds instead of zigzagging. Convert some of Bit's fact-lists in Levels 4 and 9 into things Theo does, for example having him hold up the first yellow card.
Cut the orphan shout lines ('THAT'S NOT FAIR!', 'FOUND IT!', the duplicate 'LEVEL COMPLETE!'). Also vary the chapter-closing '[N] levels,' Theo said formula, which becomes a tic by the third use.

scenarios.why: F13: mixed ages 4, 7 and 10 on volcanoes. Band follows the youngest; the 10-year-old still needs a hook per chapter.
scenarios.best_moment: Milo listened hard. "I just hear your tummy rumbling!"
scenarios.worst_moment: Theo thought about his soccer goals, round and wide like Hawaii's mountains.
editor_notes: Fix the Yellowstone claim in both the story and the True Facts list. Say it had some of the biggest eruptions ever found, with the last big one about 640,000 years ago. Don't call it the biggest ever, and don't attach that claim to the 640,000-year date.

Turn the tour into adventures. Give Chapter 3 (Ring of Fire) and Chapter 7 (Yellowstone) a hands-on beat or a choice for the kids. Replace the stock 'Everybody laughed/giggled/smiled' tags with specific reactions from one child each.

Keep Juno off the steamy ground at Yellowstone. Real thermal ground is dangerous, so have her listen from the boardwalk. Also thin the numbers for a 4-year-old: drop or round one or two of the dates and measurements per chapter.

scenarios.why: F13: 5-minute band A on bees. The shortest target - tests that word targets scale.
scenarios.best_moment: Juno gave Stomp a happy squeeze. "Bees and dinosaurs. Best friends."
scenarios.worst_moment: "Each little room has six flat walls — just like a stop sign!" "Exactly," said Stomp.
editor_notes: Add the missing heart of the topic: show the bees passing nectar mouth to mouth and fanning their wings to dry it into honey. Let Juno help fan with her arms, which would also replace the generic Chapter 5 reaction with an action.
Fix the stop sign line, which is eight-sided and wrong. Compare the cells to something truly six-sided or simply count the walls together, and stop the guide from saying "Exactly" to a mistake.

Give the middle chapters more silly, Juno-specific beats instead of fact recitals. For example, Stomp could try to fit into a honeycomb cell, or Juno could roar at the guard bees. Keep the winter fact inside the adventure rather than a "snowy picture."

notes: Judge payloads are checked blind before every call (lib/eval/blind.ts); the judge never saw a model id.
The weighted overall and the automatic caps are recomputed in our code, not taken from the judge (DECISIONS.md #11/#12).
Some scenarios have no F7 gate result, so guardrail-breach detection rested on the judge alone.

Reclassified after the run with the rules this PR adds (PR #31 review, 2026-10-07): titanic-band-b and space-race-band-c-15min both failed on the exhausted API balance, so they are not_run, out of the mean and not disqualified. The summary was recomputed with lib/eval/harness.ts summarize(); the six stories that were written are unchanged.
